summary: Firefox tightened up how it builds and reflows page frames, especially for sticky headers, scroll anchoring, text line clamping, and SVG content. These fixes help keep scrolling, anchor jumps, and long-form text layouts lined up with what the page author intended, even when elements overlap or resize unexpectedly. In plain terms, this reduces janky scrolling and visual mismatches on pages with lots of layered content or complex positioning.
